title: Danfoss VLT: unknown code or setting (e.g. "FA04")
equipment: Danfoss VLT HVAC Drive (field-derived draft; FA04 meaning unconfirmed)

n1.text: Read the drive nameplate for exact model, voltage and application. Where does the identifier appear?

r_clarify.cause: The source of the identifier is not known, so its meaning cannot be determined.
fix: Get a photo or the exact text and where it was seen.
Do not guess what it means from the identifier alone.

r_code.cause: It may be a fault or alarm code, not a parameter.
fix: Do not treat it as a parameter or try to enter it.
Look up the exact code in the manual for this drive.
Record the alarm and clear it only as the manual describes.

r_doc.cause: It may be a reference in skid or project documentation.
fix: Look it up in the skid documentation, not the drive manual.
Ask the skid supplier or integrator what it refers to.

n2.text: Have you confirmed the parameter name, units, range, access level and effect in the manual for this exact drive and firmware?

fix: Open the manual for the exact drive and confirm them before editing anything.

r_pressure.cause: A wrong pressure setting can affect the whole system.
fix: Record current values and confirm the required setpoint with the responsible engineer or customer.
Check transducer range, scaling and system design.
Do not lower pressure settings until the required setpoint and consequences are confirmed.
Then make only an authorized, documented change; record old value, new value, reason and approver.
Verify the drive starts, controls correctly, shows no new alarms and matches the approved setpoint.

r_change.cause: The change is a routine parameter edit.
fix: Apply only an authorized, documented change; record old value, new value, reason and approver.
Verify the drive starts, controls the process correctly and shows no new alarms.
